{
  "participants": [
    {
      "login": "l0rinc",
      "stance": "support",
      "note": "Concept ACK, thanked author for taking over from #35752"
    },
    {
      "login": "rkrux",
      "stance": "support",
      "note": "Concept ACK for enforcing DB error handling and memory/database consistency"
    },
    {
      "login": "jeanpablojp",
      "stance": "objection",
      "note": "Concept ACK, but raised multiple correctness concerns around DB write failure handling"
    }
  ],
  "claims": [
    {
      "id": "rc:3933080173",
      "kind": "safety",
      "harm": "failing best block write prevents BackupWallet from creating a backup file when database write failures first occur",
      "quote": "With the best block write failing, BackupWallet returns false and no copy is taken; before this change, Backup() still runs. This is the copy you most want when the database starts refusing writes.",
      "blocking": false,
      "status": "resolved",
      "author_replies": [
        "rc:3961940119"
      ],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "settled_by_id": "rc:3961940119",
      "settled_by_quote": "If a write fails, it is possible that the database is already corrupted, and we do not want to be making a backup that may not be usable."
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:3933080179",
      "kind": "correctness",
      "harm": "write failure in IncOrderPosNext leaves a half-initialized transaction in mapWallet that future calls treat as already inserted",
      "quote": "this return leaves the entry behind with no nOrderPos, no wtxOrdered slot and no AddToSpends, and every later call with the same txid then takes the !fInsertedNew path and reports success without repairing it",
      "blocking": false,
      "status": "resolved",
      "author_replies": [
        "rc:3961962437"
      ],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "settled_by_id": "rc:3961962437",
      "settled_by_quote": "This is ok, a failure here results in an exception higher up in the call stack which will result in a crash. Database write failures are supposed to be catastrophic, they are not expected to happen."
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:3933080195",
      "kind": "correctness",
      "harm": "write failure in TopUp leaves descriptor range out of sync with cache, persisting an invalid range that prevents reloading the wallet",
      "quote": "The retry then derives nothing and WriteDescriptor succeeds, persisting a range wider than the cache behind it. Reopening that wallet stops with Unable to expand wallet descriptor from cache and returns Error loading <file>: Wallet corrupted",
      "blocking": false,
      "status": "resolved",
      "author_replies": [
        "rc:3961987260"
      ],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "settled_by_id": "rc:3961987260",
      "settled_by_quote": "Write failures are supposed to be catastrophic and an indicator that corruption has likely happened."
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:3933080205",
      "kind": "correctness",
      "harm": "database write failure during wallet loading reports wallet corruption even when the root cause is a full disk",
      "quote": "On a genuinely full disk, with just enough room left for the database to open, this reports Error loading <file>: Wallet corrupted while nothing is corrupt.",
      "blocking": false,
      "status": "resolved",
      "author_replies": [
        "rc:3962002906"
      ],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "settled_by_id": "rc:3962002906",
      "settled_by_quote": "Failure to write is always corruption, regardless of how that may come about. We don't know why the write failed, it could be for reasons other than a disk being full."
    }
  ],
  "support": [
    {
      "id": "c:5320742444",
      "verdict": "Concept ACK",
      "reason": "thanks for taking over",
      "substantive": false
    },
    {
      "id": "c:5423370516",
      "verdict": "Concept ACK",
      "reason": "enforces the handling of database errors, thereby ensuring consistency between in-memory behaviour and databases behaviour",
      "substantive": true
    },
    {
      "id": "r:5111792081",
      "verdict": "Concept ACK",
      "reason": "Left some comments.",
      "substantive": false
    }
  ],
  "notes": "Initial record of PR discussion. Four concerns raised by jeanpablojp regarding in-memory rollbacks, backups, and error reporting on write failures were resolved after the author clarified that database write failures are treated as catastrophic corruptions that should abort rather than recover."
}

participants.note: Concept ACK, thanked author for taking over from #35752
Concept ACK for enforcing DB error handling and memory/database consistency
Concept ACK, but raised multiple correctness concerns around DB write failure handling

claims.harm: failing best block write prevents BackupWallet from creating a backup file when database write failures first occur
claims.quote: With the best block write failing, BackupWallet returns false and no copy is taken; before this change, Backup() still runs. This is the copy you most want when the database starts refusing writes.
claims.settled_by_quote: If a write fails, it is possible that the database is already corrupted, and we do not want to be making a backup that may not be usable.

claims.harm: write failure in IncOrderPosNext leaves a half-initialized transaction in mapWallet that future calls treat as already inserted
claims.quote: this return leaves the entry behind with no nOrderPos, no wtxOrdered slot and no AddToSpends, and every later call with the same txid then takes the !fInsertedNew path and reports success without repairing it
claims.settled_by_quote: This is ok, a failure here results in an exception higher up in the call stack which will result in a crash. Database write failures are supposed to be catastrophic, they are not expected to happen.

claims.harm: write failure in TopUp leaves descriptor range out of sync with cache, persisting an invalid range that prevents reloading the wallet
claims.quote: The retry then derives nothing and WriteDescriptor succeeds, persisting a range wider than the cache behind it. Reopening that wallet stops with Unable to expand wallet descriptor from cache and returns Error loading <file>: Wallet corrupted
claims.settled_by_quote: Write failures are supposed to be catastrophic and an indicator that corruption has likely happened.

claims.harm: database write failure during wallet loading reports wallet corruption even when the root cause is a full disk
claims.quote: On a genuinely full disk, with just enough room left for the database to open, this reports Error loading <file>: Wallet corrupted while nothing is corrupt.
claims.settled_by_quote: Failure to write is always corruption, regardless of how that may come about. We don't know why the write failed, it could be for reasons other than a disk being full.

support.reason: enforces the handling of database errors, thereby ensuring consistency between in-memory behaviour and databases behaviour

result.notes: Initial record of PR discussion. Four concerns raised by jeanpablojp regarding in-memory rollbacks, backups, and error reporting on write failures were resolved after the author clarified that database write failures are treated as catastrophic corruptions that should abort rather than recover.
